minutes.headline: Finance Committee recommended the FY2020 town budget and most money articles; building, marijuana-ban and petition articles deferred.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the public access cable budget, which is moving to an enterprise fund. It then held the Town Meeting warrant hearing, with the town manager's FY2020 budget presentation and a fuel tank cost study. It voted recommendations on the budget, stabilization, enterprise-fund and cable articles, and deferred the building, prohibition and petition articles.

public_comment.topic: Asked for added money for the school budget, which still has cuts to make.
Asked about FCC action on cable franchise funding.
Asked about the health insurance amount in the cable budget.
Fuel tank cost and return on investment.
Opposed conveying municipal land without a comprehensive plan.
Class sizes, literacy coach, librarian cut and school funding.

votes.motion: Recommend approval of the revolving funds article
Recommend approval of article 7, the budget

budget_items.what_was_said: Salaries, operations and capital are budgeted above annual revenue, with the capital portion coming from the capital fund.
Estimated cost to replace the tanks and the savings versus fuel cards were discussed.

decisions.decision: A member is assigned to write the warrant report, due April 8th.

not_audible: Several article votes had no stated tallies.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted to recommend approval of article 7, the FY2020 town budget.
It voted to recommend the revolving funds article, and later voted to recommend article 25.
It voted to defer articles 21, 22, 23 and 24, the building, marijuana-ban and petition articles.
The committee heard the public access cable budget, which is moving to an enterprise fund and is budgeted above annual revenue, with capital coming from the capital fund.
A fuel tank cost study compared replacing the tanks with fuel cards, and a member was assigned to write the warrant report, due April 8th.

why_it_matters: The recommendations shape what the Finance Committee tells Town Meeting voters about the FY2020 budget, which sets the town's spending and the tax bill that follows.
The deferred articles have no recommendation yet, so residents will not see the committee's view on them until it takes them up again.
Cable moving to an enterprise fund means its costs are meant to be met from its own revenue, so a gap between spending and revenue is a question for the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: The Finance Committee's warrant report, due April 8th.
Whether the committee takes up the deferred articles 21 to 24 again before Town Meeting.
